About This Manual 
 
This user manual provides a complete guide to using the 
Ritinjali Management Information System (MIS). 
The MIS is designed to help Ritinjali manage information 
and day-to-day operations across its school, students, 
programs, activities, and multiple branches through a 
centralized administrative system. 
This manual explains the different modules available in 
the MIS, their purpose, and the steps required to perform 
common administrative tasks.

2. Dashboard 
 
2.1 Dashboard Overview 
The Dashboard provides an overview of key student monitoring and evaluation metrics. It 
allows users to view student statistics, attendance trends, programme distribution, placement 
information, and academic-level distribution for the selected programme and date range. 
Dashboard Filters 
At the top of the dashboard, users can select: 
• Programme — Used to view dashboard information for a specific programme. 
• Date Range — Used to select the period for which the dashboard information should be 
displayed. 
Navigation Sidebar 
The sidebar provides quick access to the different sections of the Ritinjali MIS. Users can 
navigate between modules such as Dashboard, Students, Attendance, Assessments, Surveys, 
Reports, Alumni, Media, Volunteering, Exposure Visits, and Admin Panel using the sidebar 
menu. 
Tip: Use the sidebar to move between different sections of the MIS without returning to the 
dashboard.

Understanding Permission Types 
Permissions generally follow a simple structure: 
• View — Allows the user to see records and information. 
• Create — Allows the user to add new records. 
• Update — Allows the user to edit existing records. 
• Delete — Allows the user to remove records. 
• Export — Allows the user to download module data as an Excel file. 
• Manage — Provides broader administrative control over a particular area. 
• * (Wildcard) — Gives access to all permissions within that module. 
For example, attendance.* provides all available attendance permissions, while 
attendance.view only allows the user to view attendance information. 
Best Practice: Give users only the permissions required to perform their assigned 
responsibilities. Avoid providing administrative or delete permissions unless they are 
necessary.
